clue.text: It's trendy for convict to get out of trial and fine

indicators.note: the convict's word is placed out of, that is around the outside of, the words for trial and fine

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict, an old lag being a habitual prisoner
a test is a trial
fine as in slender means thin

explanation.surface: A prisoner wins release from court proceedings and walks away merely fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of' puts LAG outside TEST and THIN, giving LA + TESTTHIN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest craze or fashion item is what everyone calls trendy.

clue.text: Fielder badly wants spinner

parts.note: to want something badly is to long for it, so the clue words give longs
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is desperate to have a spin bowler on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a LONG STOP is a fielder placed directly behind the wicketkeeper; 'spinner' suggests a slow bowler but is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cricket fielding position, so the player standing there is a fielder.

clue.text: Incline to support beginner from somewhere in the Alps

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes underneath, so the word for incline sits below the one for beginner

parts.note: a tyro is a novice or beginner
to lean is to incline

explanation.surface: A novice skier is told to lean forward on some Alpine slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, so its adjective describes things from there.

clue.text: Bob came upon gang in mist

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece coming upon another is placed on top of it

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated s
a gang of workers is a team

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob stumbled across a gang of villains in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is the old shilling, abbreviated S; a shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour hanging in the air is loosely called mist or vapour.

clue.text: Student has little support when bad weather intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the weather word goes inside the support word

parts.note: a tee is the small peg supporting a golf ball
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A golfing pupil is left with little help when the storm interrupts the round.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rained-off golf lesson; 'little support' is the small peg a golfer sets the ball on, and 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being trained in a job is a learner, much like a student.

clue.text: One man in bible is burning

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the man's name is placed in the abbreviation for the bible

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, standing for the bible
Stan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A single man in the scriptures is said to be on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning can mean pressing or urgent, and an instant need is an urgent one.

clue.text: Plant contains a trace of metallic element

indicators.note: the plant's name holds within it the small piece taken from the next word

parts.note: the geranium is a garden plant

indicators.note: only a trace, the first letter, of the word metallic is used

explanation.surface: A plant is found to hold a small amount of some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metallic element' reads as one phrase, but 'metallic' only gives its first letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: This grey semiconductor metalloid is a chemical element, number 32.

clue.text: Some sausages droop

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word sausages are used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A few of the sausages are going limp.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to sink or hang down loosely, as something drooping does.

clue.text: Drunken wife carried by horse

indicators.note: the wife is carried inside the horse word, as a rider is carried by a mount

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: An intoxicated wife is being carried home on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is British slang for very drunk or intoxicated.

clue.text: Threaten to go out in the Channel

definitions.meaning: a candle flame flickers and threatens to go out when it ...
a channel for carrying away rainwater

explanation.definitionFit: A dying candle flame flickers, and a roadside drain is a channel.

clue.text: Feature about king of the Vikings

indicators.note: the facial feature goes about, around, the letter for king

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A characteristic of a Viking king is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the language of the Scandinavian seafarers, so the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Missing catching ball that's soaking

indicators.note: the word for missing catches, holds inside it, the ball word

parts.note: missing means absent
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A fielder misses a catch and the ball is soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaking up liquid, like a sponge, is called absorbent.

clue.text: A canal Sam renovated in Spain

indicators.note: renovated suggests something rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Sam has had a canal restored on the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a historic university city located in western Spain.

clue.text: Porter about to live in Poplar

indicators.note: the drink goes about, around, the verb meaning to live

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so ale
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A doorman is set to move to Poplar, a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is an East London district, but here it is the tree; the white poplar is called an ABELE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the white poplar, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Radical brute with a past

parts.note: an ox is a brute beast
late can mean former or past, as in the late president

explanation.surface: A political extremist is described as a beast with a history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' suggests politics, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry this salt-forming ion of oxalic acid counts as a radical.

clue.text: Despondent when a boat blew about

indicators.note: about here means in disarray or around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast when the wind blew their boat around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a dejected, depressed state is idiomatically like the sea at low tide.

clue.text: Train makes Turkish leader feel off colour

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Turkish

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell or off colour

explanation.surface: A train journey leaves the Turkish leader feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway but is the long trailing part of a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown's train is the long part trailing behind, as is a tail.

clue.text: Impose a curfew on office of proverbial confidant

parts.note: in British schools and colleges to gate someone is to confine them as a punishment
a post is an office or position

explanation.surface: An official confines someone to the office while sharing secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'between you, me and the gatepost' means told in confidence, making the gatepost the proverbial confidant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a fence upright as the silent sharer of secrets.

clue.text: Pagan I get on with by and by

parts.note: do can mean fare or get on, as in how are you doing
by and by means later on

explanation.surface: A heathen promises to get along with others eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol worshipper is a pagan or heathen.

clue.text: Fight for breath while doctor comes round

indicators.note: the doctor's letters come round, enclose, the word for while

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
as can mean while, as in as I was walking

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to breathe while the doctor visits.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to struggle for air with sudden short breaths.

clue.text: An artist measures likewise

parts.note: a pica is a printer's unit of type measurement
so can mean likewise, as in so do I

explanation.surface: A painter takes measurements in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Cannonade has dismal crowd retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole run of both words is read in reverse

parts.note: drab means dull or dismal
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A gloomy crowd falls back under heavy artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to attack with sustained artillery fire, which a cannonade is.

clue.text: Heckle barristers over persecution

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another sits on top of it

parts.note: the bar is the collective name for barristers
the rack was an instrument of torture, so persecution

explanation.surface: Lawyers shout down someone being victimised.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is British for jeering at a speaker or player, much like heckling.

clue.text: Doctor in storm hazard

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go in the word for storm

parts.note: a gale is a storm
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor out in a storm is in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to risk or bet it, which is to take a chance.

clue.text: Wine stored in port, aged

indicators.note: the wine is placed inside the abbreviation for port

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Wine kept in a harbour cellar has matured.
explanation.definitionFit: Too old to function well is an informal sense of aged.

clue.text: One hit nothing in battle

parts.note: one can be read as the article a
to lam is to beat or hit
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A single soldier scored no hits during the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was the 1836 siege in the Texas Revolution, a famous battle.

clue.text: Soldier without energy is not spiritual

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the soldier goes outside the energy letter

parts.note: a corporal is a soldier, a junior NCO
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soldier who lacks energy shows no sign of a soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion signal but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bodily or physical belongs to the material world rather than the spirit.

clue.text: In the old days entertained union leader at the right moment

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so the old days word takes the leader inside

parts.note: once means formerly, in the old days

indicators.note: the leader of the word union is its first letter

explanation.surface: In days gone by a trade union boss was wined and dined.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer arriving on their prompt comes in exactly when needed.

clue.text: Cricketer meets pithy American in London

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer
terse means brief and pithy

explanation.surface: A batsman runs into a curt American in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERSEA is a district of south London; 'Cricketer' suggests BATTER, which leaves an unusable SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This riverside district, home to a famous power station, lies in the capital.

clue.text: Influence of Tory boor

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a lout is a boor

explanation.surface: A Conservative yob wields power.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for power or influence, especially political.

clue.text: Amphibian that's agile died off

indicators.note: off signals that the died letter is taken away from the word for agile

parts.note: deft means nimble or agile

explanation.surface: A nimble creature from the pond has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt, especially a young one, is a small amphibian.

clue.text: Check mail appearing in print

parts.note: to block is to check or stop
a letter is a piece of mail

explanation.surface: A censor inspects post that is about to be published.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitals written separately, as on forms, are what is asked for by please print.
